messages:
kevin: Heads-up — seeing a p99 latency spike in prod after today's onboard (checkpoint v3.4 + tokenizer PR). CI perf also failed. Anyone else seeing this?

anna: Yep. p50 looks fine but p99 jumped from ~180ms -> ~560ms on coralv4 pools. KV cache evictions shot up. Dashboard: https://dash.redd/inference/perf/2176654321 

sanjay: Noted. Both tokenizer change (PR #4287) and a batch-heuristic tweak (PR #4290) landed within minutes. Starting a local bisect now.

ci-bot: CI - perf/regressions/2176654321 failed — p99 increase +82%. Artifact: /artifacts/perf-2176654321.json

maria: I can repro locally when I combine v3.4 checkpoint + the tokenizer change. Token counts are ~1.7x due to extra EOS/pad handling; sample-rate metrics shift. Kernel selection log shows fallback to a slower kernel for longer sequences.

maria: ```
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] kernel_select: model=checkpoint_v3.4 seq_len=384 padding_ratio=0.22 -> selected_kernel=gpu_fallback_cublas
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] kvcache: hit_rate=0.65 -> 0.30
```

kevin: Can we bisect which merge is the bigger offender? Revert tokenizer first?

anna: Quick local bisect results: revert tokenizer PR -> p99 back to baseline. Apply batch-heuristic tweak alone -> small p99 bump (~10%). Both together -> large regression. So tokenizer increases avg seq len and the heuristic picks the slow kernel and disables the fast KV prefix path.

sanjay: Hypothesis: the batch heuristic uses a sample_rate metric derived from the tokenizer output. The tokenizer drift increased padding/EOS so sample_rate exceeds the heuristic threshold; runtime chooses a route that disables dense batching and some KV prefix matching, causing thrash.

maria: Profiling traces confirm that: KV cache miss rate went from ~3% -> ~33% and batch coalescing rate dropped ~40%. Flame graph + traces: https://profiling.redd/v/2176654321

kevin: Suggested action items: 1) rollback tokenizer PR in prod (canary first), 2) add CI perf test for token-length histogram and kernel-route invariants, 3) add a runtime guard so kernel route flip requires both sample_rate AND sustained seq_len change.

anna: I'm opening the rollback PR now and will push to canary at 10% traffic. Will also add a CI perf job that computes token length hist and asserts no >15% delta from baseline.

sanjay: I'll add a small change to the runtime: if avg_seq_len > X OR padding_ratio > Y alone, don't flip kernel route — require both or N minutes of sustained signal. Also add telemetry alert when kvcache_hit_rate drops >5% over 5m.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback PR merged to canary at 2176657321 — traffic=10% — healthchecks=passing

kevin: Canary looks good so far — p99 back to expected on canary. We'll validate for 30m then promote to prod.

maria: After rollback, we should also run a short e2e against checkpoint v3.5 and add a changelog note for tokenizer sampling semantics.

kevin: Agreed. Thanks all — keep an eye on dashboards and CI.
